headline: Recommended changing a deed restriction at 185 High Rock Rd, delaying its claw back deadline to April 1, 2026.
summary: The owner asked to push back the deadline for demolishing the existing house on the lot, which has already been torn down. The deed must be amended before a new house can be built.
decisions: Recommended approval of petition 215-25 to change the claw back deadline at 185 High Rock Rd, passed by unanimous consent.

decision_evidence.quote: A motion was made by Councilor Green to recommend Approval of the petition, seconded by Councilor Cragin. The motion passed by unanimous consent.

decision_titles: Claw back deadline change at 185 High Rock Rd
plain_text:
pg. 1 
Meeting Minutes of the 
City Property Committee of the Fitchburg City Council 
for 
Tuesday, January 6, 2026 
 
Chairperson Van Hazinga called the meeting to order at approximately 6:30 p.m. in the Legislative 
Building at 700 Main Street, Fitchburg, MA.   
 
Members Present: Members Absent: 
Councilor Andrew Van Hazinga, Chair Councilor Paul Beauchemin 
Councilor Sally Cragin  
Councilor Amy Green 
 
Other City Officials Present: 
Councilor Marisa Fleming, Petitioner 
 
Public Comment: 
 
None  
 
Minutes 
 
Motion by Councilor Green, seconded by Councilo r Cragin, to approve the minutes from the 
meeting on December 10, 2025.  The motion passed by unanimous consent.   
 
Agenda Items: 
 
215-25  Councilor Fleming on behalf of Eduard  Gukasov, the curren t owner of 185 High 
Rock Rd is requesting a modification to the claw back provis ion of the property 
deed as outlined in the enclosed petition.  
 
Chair Van Hazinga explained that the property was sold by the City of Fitchburg in January 2024 
with a deed restriction that the existing improvements be demolished and removed within one year.  
If violated, the City can take back the property and the owner loses the $41,000 they paid for the 
property.  The owner is asking that the deadline fo r the claw back restriction to delayed till April 
1, 2026.  It appears that the existing house has been demolished, but the deed restriction still needs 
to be amended before the owner can build a house on the site.  
 
Vote:  A motion was made by Councilor Green to recommend Approval of the petition, seconded 
by Councilor Cragin.  The motion passed by unanimous consent.   
 
Adjournment 
 
Councilor Green moved to adjourn the meeting and Councilor Cragin seconded the motion, which 
passed by unanimous consent.  The City Property Committee of the City Council adjourned at 
approximately 6:39 pm. 
 
A video recording can be viewed at www.fatv.org:  City Property Committee 01.06.2026 
 
Minutes prepared by Councilor Van Hazinga, Committee Chair.
